I think this is a deletable test, but if we really want to keep it, what about this: add an `*int` testing knob that is incremented if non-nil every time we get a chunk completed event in the backup job before we pass it to the progress logger, and then we just assert it is >0 after just  running a vanilla backup (doing away with the req filter, all the job update tuning, etc needed to observe the job change mid-execution)

> I think this is a deletable test, but if we really want to keep it, what about this: add an *int testing knob that is incremented if non-nil every time we get a chunk completed event in the backup job before we pass it to the progress logger, and then we just assert it is >0 after just running a vanilla backup (doing away with the req filter, all the job update tuning, etc needed to observe the job change mid-execution)

Yup, similar to what I was thinking. I was thinking of a hook in the progress logger but that we call after Report so that we could use it to coordinate checking that the job state was updated as expected.

Eh, I'm thinking simpler: just check that we completed spans in the backup side, and leave testing ChunkProgressLogger to the jobs package if we really think we need to test writing a float to a proto. Lamme take a stab at this.

review_comments: I like the idea that we can reduce the size of the test.  It could be worth a comment though on vaguely what conditions ensure that we get a set of of todoSpans that allow this test to record incremental progress in the way we expect.  Or perhaps a testing hook that gets passed the backup plan spec so that we could make some basic assertions about the number of backup spans assigned to the processor so that if it changes this test will be easier to debug.

Logging suggests that since we backup >6 system tables we are guaranteed to send atleast 6 ExportRequests, one for each table. I've added a blurb above the test about this and an alternative if this assumption were to change. Let me know if its clearer!
